title: Var-JEPA: A Variational Formulation of the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture – Bridging Predictive and Generative Self-Supervised Learning
claim: The standard deterministic architecture is a special case of a probabilistic one; adding stochastic encoders and decoders unifies it under one objective.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, left-to-right flows, shared color-coded legend strip below
description: Two side-by-side block diagrams compare the baseline JEPA (left) with Var-JEPA (right). Each is drawn as gray bands with colored rounded boxes and arrows. In JEPA, context x passes through an encoder to s_x. A predictor g(s_x, z) then outputs a predicted target representation. Target y passes through its own encoder to s_y, and a prediction loss and a surrogate cost sit at the end. A small orange latent z feeds the predictor. Var-JEPA is much denser. Deterministic encoders become inference networks q(s_x|x), q(z|s_x) and q(s_y|s_x,y,z). The predictor becomes a generative network p(s_y|s_x,z). Decoders p(x|s_x) and p(y|s_y) are added. Several green KL, reconstruction and generation loss boxes appear. A color legend at the bottom maps shapes and colors to roles: encoder, prediction network, generative network, loss and latent variable.
caption: Comparison between JEPA (left) and Var-JEPA (right). Var-JEPA extends JEPA by replacing deterministic encoders and predictor with probabilistic distributions, and adding generative networks (decoders) to enable variational learning under a unified ELBO.
abstract: The Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) is often seen as a non-generative alternative to likelihood-based self-supervised learning, emphasizing prediction in representation space rather than reconstruction in observation space. We argue that the resulting separation from probabilistic generative modeling is largely rhetorical rather than structural: the canonical JEPA design (coupled encoders with a context-to-target predictor) mirrors the variational posteriors and learned conditional priors obtained when variational inference is applied to a particular class of coupled latent-variable models, and standard JEPA can be viewed as a deterministic specialization in which regularization is imposed via architectural and training heuristics rather than an explicit likelihood. Building on this view, we derive the Variational JEPA (Var-JEPA), which makes the latent generative structure explicit by optimizing a single Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO). This yields meaningful representations without ad-hoc anti-collapse regularizers and allows principled uncertainty quantification in the latent space. We instantiate the framework for tabular data (Var-T-JEPA) and achieve strong representation learning and downstream performance, improving over T-JEPA across real-world tabular benchmarks while remaining competitive with strong raw-feature baselines.
